title: Open cover detection and descent of etale origin
statement: Let X be a scheme and (U_i) any open cover of X [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For fixed module-valued pro-etale sheaves, restriction to all U_i jointly detects zero sheaves and zero derived objects. Write nu_X^* and R nu_X,* for the ordinary etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. If R is a complex of pro-etale module sheaves, R nu_X,* R is bounded below, and each restriction R|U_i is isomorphic to nu_U_i^* N_i for some etale complex N_i, then the actual comparison counit nu_X^* R nu_X,* R -> R is invertible. These are the existing source-library open-cover theorems; no boundedness of R or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The open family belongs to the pro-etale precoverage. On every site object its base changes give a covering sieve. A map invertible on all restrictions is therefore invertible. Apply this to a zero map into the zero sheaf; apply homology to deduce zero detection for derived objects. This is the existing proved Conservative section.

Take the cone C of the comparison counit. The bounded-below comparison unit is invertible, so R nu_* C is zero. On each open, maps from complexes of etale origin to C vanish by the open extension-by-zero adjunction and its compatibility with comparison. In the restricted counit triangle both first terms have etale origin. Its second arrow and its shift vanish, forcing C|U_i to be zero. The preceding cover detection makes C zero; hence the actual counit is invertible. This is the existing proved Gluing section.
